chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad who said:

I read the emancipation deed of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and behold its text was: 'This is what Ja'far ibn Muhammad has emancipated — he freed so-and-so, his slave, for the face of Allah, not intending by it any recompense nor thanks, upon (the stipulation) that he establish the salat, give the zakat, perform the Hajj of the House, fast the month of Ramadan, befriend the friends of Allah, and disavow the enemies of Allah.' Witnessed by so-and-so, and so-and-so, and so-and-so — three (of them).

key_terms.شُكُور: Thanks/gratitude — acknowledgment or gratitude from the freed person
key_terms.عِتْق: Emancipation/manumission — the legal act of freeing an enslaved person under Islamic law
key_terms.لِوَجْهِ اللَّهِ: For the face/sake of Allah — sincerely for God, without worldly motivation
key_terms.يَتَبَرَّأَ مِنْ أَعْدَاءِ اللَّهِ: To disavow the enemies of Allah — bara'a, dissociation from those who oppose Allah and His Imams
key_terms.يَتَوَلَّى أَوْلِيَاءَ اللَّهِ: To befriend the friends of Allah — walaya, the Shia concept of loyalty to the Imams

ai.seo_question: What conditions did Imam al-Sadiq place in his slave emancipation deed?
ai.summary: This narration preserves the actual emancipation (manumission) deed of Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), showing how he freed a slave for the sake of Allah alone, without any expectation of reward or gratitude. The deed uniquely stipulates that the freed slave must observe the five pillars — prayer, zakat, Hajj, fasting — and embrace the Shia doctrine of walaya (loyalty to Allah's friends) and bara'a (disavowal of His enemies). This document illustrates that Imam al-Sadiq framed emancipation as a spiritually and doctrinally transformative act, integrating legal manumission with religious commitment. The phrase 'for the face of Allah, not intending recompense nor thanks' directly echoes Quran 76:9, reflecting the Imam's application of Quranic piety to legal documents.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Ibrahim Bin Abu Al Balaad who said,

‘I read the emancipation (deed) of Abu Abdullahasws, for its starting was – ‘This is what Ja’farasws Bin Muhammadasws has emancipated, an emancipation of so and so slave of hisasws for the Face of Allahazwj, not intending by it a Recompense, nor thanks, upon (the stipulation) that he would establish the Prayer, and give the Zakat, and perform Hajj of the House (Kabah), and Fast the Month of Ramazan, and would befriend the friends of Allahazwj and would disavow (reject) from Hisazwj enemies’. Testified by so and so, and so and so, and so and so’ – Three (of them)’.
